description:
Contexter is memory that stays the same in every AI you use. What you save in ChatGPT is there when you open Claude or write to the Telegram bot, and what arrives in Telegram is there for ChatGPT. No copying, no explaining the project again in a new chat.

How it works
- Save a result of your work (a plan, a list, a summary, a decision) into a context: a folder for one project or idea.
- Add notes, photos and files from Telegram: send them to the bot, or let it collect a group chat you have joined.
- Ask about a context in any assistant and continue where you stopped yesterday, even if that was a different AI.
- Share a context with a person: they read it in their own AI, and both of you add to it.

What ChatGPT can do with Contexter connected
- list your contexts and show what each one holds;
- read a context's records and answer from them;
- save a result into a context, or update a saved list instead of making a second copy;
- tell you who will see a record before it lands in a shared context;
- send a result into a Telegram group chat you take part in, or post an invitation link so the people there can join a shared context, both only when you ask for it.

What Contexter never does
Nothing is saved silently: every write happens on your explicit request. Deletions are reversible for 7 days. Shared contexts always show their audience. Nothing is collected from your conversation beyond what you ask to save.

Show my latest context in Contexter as a card
